title: vLLM 0.31: Keep Model Weights Across Restarts - AI Daily Diff Oct 5
closing_line: Check compatibility before testing a restart. Follow AI Daily Diff for useful AI repositories and their limits.

items.headline: vLLM 0.31 adds a command to keep model weights across engine restarts.
items.what_changed: The October 5 release adds vllm preload, launching a persistent GPU weight-cache daemon.
items.why_it_matters: Serving operators can evaluate skipping repeated weight loading when restarting an engine.
items.who_should_care: Developers operating GPU model servers, with Linux and model-loading experience.

diff.minus: A normal restart loads model weights again.
diff.plus: A compatible restarting engine can reuse weights retained by a separate daemon.

items.watch_out: CUDA or ROCm only. Keep the daemon alive in zero-copy mode; no live restart benchmark here.

walkthrough.use_case: Inspect a restart path that reuses already-loaded model weights.
walkthrough.steps:
Install vLLM 0.31.0 for your compatible GPU stack; obtain an accessible checkpoint.
Follow the guide: vllm preload --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --tensor-parallel-size 4
Then: vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --tensor-parallel-size 4 --load-format ipc_cache
This documented example requires four compatible GPUs and access to the named model.
walkthrough.availability: Linux, Python 3.10-3.13 and sufficient GPU memory. Apache-2.0 repository; model access and licenses are separate.
walkthrough.limitations: Same user/node and matching configuration required; incompatible cache may fall back to disk. No pipeline parallelism or zero-copy sleep mode. No live test.
walkthrough.evidence_label: Version-pinned documentation reviewed; no live GPU test.

youtube_description:
vLLM 0.31.0 adds a preload command for keeping model weights available across serving-engine restarts. This artifact review explains the operator task, the documented starting path and the conditions to check before evaluation.

The October 5 release is the new event. We reviewed the pinned release, README, Apache-2.0 license and setup documentation; we did not run GPU inference or measure restart time.

Start from a compatible Linux GPU environment and an accessible model checkpoint. Read the version-pinned preload guide before trying the daemon and serving commands. The linked sample is documentation, not a tested deployment recipe for every machine.

This is about restarting a serving engine, not better model answers or a promised throughput gain. Model licenses remain separate from the serving repository. Follow AI Daily Diff for verified builder tools and practical evaluation questions.

Preload guide: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.31.0/features/preload/
Repository and license: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/v0.31.0
